title: Simple Past or Present Perfect: Time, Completion, Signal Words

vocabulary.meaning_en: the third verb form: worked, gone, been, eaten
a verb whose past ends in -ed: work – worked – worked
a verb with special past forms: go – went – gone
the period of time when something happens
vocabulary.example: The time frame of the present perfect is "in my life".
"Yesterday" is a specific point in time.
Both tenses show completion, but in different ways.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a word that shows which tense to use
vocabulary.example: "Yesterday" is a signal word for the simple past.

vocabulary.note_en: Usually at the end of the sentence.

vocabulary.example: I have never been to Japan.
Have you ever been to Asia?
I visited my uncle last week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: at some time from birth until now
vocabulary.example: I have been to Tokyo once in my life.

fine_lines.title: I was in Tokyo two years ago vs I have been to Tokyo
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الماضي البسيط: نقطة محددة في الزمن (two years ago) والحدث انتهى ولا علاقة له بالآن. المضارع التام: حدث في وقت ما في حياتي (غير محدد)، وله أهمية للحديث الآن.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Simple past: a specific point in time (two years ago); finished and cut off from now. Present perfect: some time in my life (not specific), and it matters to the conversation now.

examples.sentence: I was in Tokyo two years ago.
Have you been to Asia? Yes, I have been to Tokyo.

fine_lines.title: yet vs already
fine_lines.explanation_ar: yet في النفي والسؤال (لم يحدث بعد): I haven't eaten yet. already في الإثبات (حدث قبل الآن): I have already eaten.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Yet" in negatives and questions (not done until now): I haven't eaten yet. "Already" in positives (done before now): I have already eaten.

examples.sentence: I have already finished my homework.

expressions.meaning_en: Did you eat before now? (Maybe I'll offer you food.)
expressions.example: I just cooked some chicken. Have you eaten yet?

expressions.meaning_en: Until now, I have not had food.
expressions.example: I was working all day, so I haven't eaten yet.
Have you ever been to Asia?

grammar.title: Form
grammar.explanation_ar: الماضي البسيط: الفعل في صيغة الماضي ونفس الشكل لكل الضمائر (I/she/they worked). المضارع التام: have/has + التصريف الثالث (I have worked, she has worked, he has gone).
grammar.explanation_en: Simple past: the past form, the same for all subjects (I/she/they worked). Present perfect: have/has + past participle (I have worked, she has worked, he has gone).

grammar.title: 1) Time frame
grammar.explanation_ar: الماضي البسيط = نقطة محددة في الماضي (SP = Specific Point): yesterday, one hour ago, on March 14th. المضارع التام = في وقت ما من حياتي، غير محدد، لكنه مهم الآن.
grammar.explanation_en: Simple past = a specific point in the past (SP = Specific Point): yesterday, one hour ago, on March 14th. Present perfect = some time in my life, not specific, but important now.
examples: I was in Tokyo two years ago.

grammar.title: 2) Completion
grammar.explanation_ar: في الماضي البسيط نعرف متى انتهى الحدث وهو مقطوع عن الحاضر. في المضارع التام لا نعرف متى انتهى، لكن له أثر على الآن.
grammar.explanation_en: In the simple past we know when the action finished, and it is cut off from now. In the present perfect we don't know when it finished, but it affects now.
examples: I ate five minutes ago. (finished, no effect now)
I have already eaten. (so I don't want food now)

grammar.title: 3) Signal words
grammar.explanation_ar: كلمات الماضي البسيط: yesterday, two minutes ago, a week ago, last week. كلمات المضارع التام: yet, already, never, ever.
grammar.explanation_en: Simple past signal words: yesterday, two minutes ago, a week ago, last week. Present perfect signal words: yet, already, never, ever.
examples: I have never told you this.
